text:
marta: FYI customer in APAC sees intermittent failures when calling hosted inference from behind a corporate outbound proxy + allowlist. Only outbound to their proxy (443) is allowed, and their firewall enforces hostname-based allowlists at the proxy.

kyle: what errors are they seeing? 502s, TLS, CONNECT blocked?

marta: mostly CONNECT failures and short lived 502/504. Their proxy logs show 403/blocked for some CONNECT attempts, but not all — looks flaky.

ben: two quick suspects: (1) proxy is doing SNI-based allowlist but some client connections are not preserving SNI (e.g., HTTP/2 or connection reuse weirdness), (2) SNAT port churn from their NAT causing proxy session tracking to drop mid-session.

carla: also check DNS path. If their proxy resolves hostnames differently or we send requests to different hostnames (model variants like model-v2.redwood-inference.internal) it could trip rules. Do they only allow a single hostname?

dylan: can we ask them to grep proxy logs for the exact Host/SNI values on the rejected CONNECTs? that will tell whether our clients are using multiple hostnames or switching SNI mid-stream.

marta: asked for logs, they provided snippet: 

infra-bot: [log snippet pasted by customer]

"CONNECT model.prod.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1" 403 - "no-sni-match"
"CONNECT model-eu1.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1" 200 -
"CONNECT model.prod.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1" 403 - "session-reset"

ben: that shows two different hostnames (model.prod vs model-eu1). If their allowlist only permits model-eu1.redwood.ai (or a single entry), connections to the other hostname will be rejected.

kyle: given we have multi-region routing and can fall back between endpoints, try telling the customer to: 1) whitelist the wildcard SNI/hostnames we use (*.redwood-inference.com or specific hostnames we gave them), 2) allow HTTP CONNECT to arbitrary hostnames on 443 so TLS SNI is preserved, OR 3) route our traffic through a static egress IP/project that they can allow.

carla: practical sample to reproduce (ask them to run from an internal host behind the proxy):

```
# test direct CONNECT through proxy and inspect SNI
curl -v -x http://their-proxy.internal:3128 https://model.prod.redwood.ai/health
```

carla: if the proxy returns 403 above, check whether it rewrites SNI or forces a Host header to some internal value — we need the proxy to do pure CONNECT passthrough for TLS.

marta: customer also mentioned they perform TLS inspection (MITM) in some cases. that breaks certificate pinning and may upset our client health checks. need explicit guidance for them.

dylan: for TLS inspection customers: either disable deep inspect for our hostnames (allow CONNECT passthrough), or if they must MITM, add our CA to the trusted chain and allow the inspected certificate to present the original SNI. honestly we prefer passthrough.

ben: additional note on SNAT churn: if their NAT reassigns ephemeral source ports aggressively, some long-lived connections or reused connections could appear as different sessions to the proxy and get rate-limited/blocked. two mitigation options: assign a stable NAT pool for hosts that talk to us, or relax the proxy session affinity for those clients.

marta: asked them if they can pin a small set of egress IPs. they said firewall policy won't allow IP-based allowlist except for a managed set. they asked if we can provide region-specific stable egress IPs for their account.

kyle: we can offer dedicated egress IPs via a reserved dedicated pool for Dedicated/Private customers — ops-team can confirm availability and cost. for hosted customers, suggest wildcard SNI + CONNECT passthrough as first step.

carla: minimal allowlist checklist to share with customer: 
- Permit HTTP CONNECT to destination port 443 (do not terminate TLS)
- Whitelist SNI/Hostnames used by us: e.g., model.prod.redwood.ai, model-eu1.redwood.ai, and any region hostnames we provided (or use *.redwood-inference.com)
- If TLS inspection is required: import our root CA into proxy trust store and allow original SNI header to be preserved
- If IP-based allowlist is required: request managed egress IP pool from Redwood support and add those IP(s) to their firewall

marta: shared checklist and also asked for a short sampling of rejected CONNECTs (full lines). customer will send more.

dylan: if they send full headers, also ask for the proxy product/version (squid/bluecoat/panos) — some proxies rewrite SNI for http2 or block CONNECT reuse.

ben: small debugging trick they can run from inside to confirm whether SNI is present: 

```
openssl s_client -connect their-proxy:3128 -quiet
# then issue a CONNECT manually and watch the TLS handshake to see SNI
```

marta: great. I'll loop in solutions and offer the dedicated egress IP option if they can't change proxy rules. thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: note added to ticket INF-4729 (egress allowlist -> recommend SNI wildcard or managed egress IP).
